ddx.step1_summary:
• Chief complaint: Acute breathing difficulty 15 min after a wasp sting while gardening.
• Symptoms: – Onset: sudden, within minutes of sting.
  – Duration: ongoing for ~15 min when call placed.
  – Character/severity: shallow breathing, chest tightness; tingling sensation in lips; blotchy skin rash; denies throat closing; no prior similar episodes.
  – Aggravating/alleviating factors: triggered by wasp sting; no medications taken yet.
• Past medical history: Eczema; allergic to penicillin; history of aerosinusitis when flying. No asthma or other chronic disease reported.
• Medications/allergies: Uses antihistamines PRN for flying; allergy to penicillin; no regular daily meds stated.
• Family/social history: Married; wife at home; was gardening outdoors; no smoking/alcohol history provided.
• Vital signs/exam findings: Remote visit—no vitals measured. Subjective findings: shallow breathing, chest tightness, tingling lips, blotchy rash; no noted lip/throat swelling; no wheeze reported on auscultation (none possible remotely).
• Labs/imaging: None.

V: Angioedema (vascular permeability leading to lip/throat swelling)—can follow insect stings.
I: Local cellulitis or toxic reaction at sting site—could present later but less likely for immediate systemic symptoms.
D: Underlying COPD/asthma (degenerative airway disease) exacerbated by stress/allergen, though history absent.
I2: Toxic reaction to wasp venom (non-IgE–mediated mast-cell degranulation).
C: Congenital reactive airway disease (e.g., undiagnosed asthma) triggered by irritant.
A: Anaphylaxis secondary to wasp sting—classic immediate multisystem allergic reaction.
T: Traumatic anxiety-induced hyperventilation following painful sting.
E: Acute panic attack (stress-related catecholamine surge causing dyspnoea and tingling).

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Immediate onset after sting with respiratory involvement and cutaneous findings fits classic early anaphylaxis; clinician advised emergency services.
Cutaneous blotchy rash and lip tingling suggest generalized histamine release, but airway compromise not yet definitive.
Acute stressful event could provoke shallow breathing and tingling, yet presence of rash points to allergic cause.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Asthma or reactive airway exacerbation triggered by allergen
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Chest tightness fits bronchospasm, but no asthma history or wheeze reported.
